answer: Every epoch, a prism of five verifier nodes on different continents fires timed pings at each identity, a scheme called latency triangulation. A valid reply carries a pigment: the ping nonce signed with that identity's key. Each ping's voyage time caps how far the replier can sit from that verifier. Fakes sharing one server show the same five-way delay fingerprint and merge into one seat, so each fake must rent its own host in a distinct city, about $5 a month, paid even if never flagged; 500 fakes cost $2,500 monthly. Proxies only add delay.
